correctness.rationale: The literal basis product gives XY=r(X)c(Y)^T. The row/column map onto the common-total hyperplane has the stated linear section in all characteristics and kernel W. Testing pure nonzero row and column profiles shows the center equals W, which annihilates on both sides. For a mixed profile the commutation equation forces simultaneous proportionality; pure nonzero profiles have U or V as their centralizer, and each such centralizer is commutative. This gives the maximal subalgebras, dimensions and mixed-line count. For any tuple either a mixed column forces all profiles onto its line, or all nonzero profiles lie in a common pure family. After a linear splitting the rank-one locus is the irreducible determinantal variety times W^t; a pure locus is absorbed exactly when its profile dimension is one, since t≥2. The dimension equalities reduce to (n-2)(t-1)=2 for m=2<n and (m-2)(t-2)=2 for m=n≥3, giving the stated exceptions. Counting disjoint nonzero mixed-line tuples and the two pure families with their shared zero, then lifting q^(wt)-fold, gives all arities including t=1. No conclusion on the raw scheme follows or is claimed. The frozen verify.py checks literal products in three small cases, counts tuples via profile enumeration and fiber sizes, and checks two literal-product maximal-clique cases over F_2. It was read, not executed; it is finite corroboration only.

evidence: The census proves that a zero profile commutes with all profiles, a nonzero pure profile exactly with its own pure space, and a mixed one exactly with its scalar multiples of the same mixed profile. The argument uses nonzero outer factors and a common sum; q appears only when counting solutions.
Translated from profiles, the pure centralizers are exactly U and V, and the mixed centralizers are exactly the preimages of the mixed lines.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Every noncentral centralizer described in that proof is already a pairwise-commuting algebra, so these are the maximal ones; a center-only subalgebra cannot be maximal. For arbitrary t, one nonzero mixed profile then forces rank at most one, while without a mixed profile two opposite pure types cannot be present. This gives rank-at-most-one union the two linear spaces over every algebraic closure. The standard dimension d+t-1 of the rank-one locus, and containment of a pure locus just when its profile dimension is one, give the dimensions and the asserted list by equating them. Finally the same families contribute two full pure spaces with one common zero and q^t-1 nonzero tuples per mixed line. Thus the main assertions do not require a new structural input beyond the available exact pair relation.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed commutator-rank census does more than print the same t=2 count: its proof solves the commutation equation by exact profiles in the identical algebra. Those solutions are the pure profile spaces, mixed lines, and the unrestricted fiber for the zero profile, exactly the decisive classification used here. The proof is field-independent up to the final counting, and the all-arity union then follows immediately by selecting a mixed entry or ruling out opposite pure types. The ensuing dimensions, exceptional list and counts are standard rank-one geometry and arithmetic on those same fibers. The full tuple theorem is not printed verbatim there, but its asserted distinctions are mechanical consequences of the available description, not new structure beyond it. This evaluates distinct coverage, not which dated catalog entry was first derived.
residual_risks: Derivation independence and chronological order are unresolved; the close census entry has a later catalog date than the frozen entry. The decision relies on equivalent structural coverage in the current evidence.
A dedicated older Munn-algebra search was not completed; Matrix semigroups with commutable rank (10.1007/s00233-002-0013-5) did not yield a readable primary copy and contributes no negative evidence.

value.rationale: The object is classical and the many commuting linear families contrast meaningfully with the absence of commuting distinct elements in the original band. The all-arity decomposition is useful structural information: it shows when the pure loci persist as distinct components and exactly when the resulting geometry is equidimensional. This evaluates the significance of the classification itself, not a purported new pair count or any priority over the equivalent profile description.
